Emily / Oliver —

Appreciate the clarifications — very helpful. Short answers to help procurement: 

- Hosted API (redwood-hosted endpoints): can be region-scoped (EU-only processing) but by default telemetry and some control-plane metadata are aggregated across regions unless we add strict contractual controls and technical isolation. For PHI workloads we typically recommend Dedicated or Private because they provide stronger guarantees and isolation.

- Dedicated capacity (EU): supports reserved GPU pools in an EU region with VPC peering options. This meets EU data residency for processing and storage and keeps compute tenancy dedicated to your workloads. It is the lowest-friction path to compliance with moderate additional cost vs Hosted.

- Private (customer-managed VPC / on-prem): offers the strongest control — everything runs inside your VPC (or on-prem) and we deliver a private control plane. This is the best option if legal requires no shared control-plane telemetry or if there are additional network egress constraints. It is highest effort to set up and has different support/responsibility splits.

- Backups / DR: If backups contain PHI they must stay in the EU. For Dedicated we can configure backup targets in the EU only; for Private you control backup targets. Cross-region replication with PHI would require explicit contractual approval and is not recommended by default.

Action items from our side (what we’ll deliver before the next call):
1) Dylan: TCO sketch comparing A (Dedicated EU + VPC peering) vs B (Private EU VPC). Include expected latency bands and a 12-month cost estimate.
2) Mina: compile SOC 2 + subprocessor list + network diagram template and an example KMS integration note.
3) Jordan: draft a short runbook for onboarding and maintenance responsibilities per deployment mode.

Proposed follow-up: Thu 18 Sep, 10:00–10:30 CET. Dylan will lead the network/peering section.

If that time works, I’ll send a calendar invite and attach the matrix and the residency sheet once you’ve filled it.

Thanks — Jordan
